authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Titan America completed its IPO of 24,000,000 common shares at $16.00 per share, generating proceeds of approximately $136.8 million after underwriting discounts and commissions.
The STET segment was divested to Titan Cement Netherlands B.V., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the parent Titan SA.
The company completed its acquisition of Keystone Cement. The acquired assets contributed revenue to the Mid-Atlantic segment in Q3 2026.

business_model.claim: Titan America is a vertically integrated maker and supplier of heavy building materials, operating mainly in Florida and the Mid-Atlantic, including Metro New York, Virginia and the Carolinas.
quotes: Titan America is a leading vertically integrated, multi-regional manufacturer and supplier of heavy building materials and services operating primarily in Florida, the New York and New Jersey Metropolitan area (“Metro New York”), Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina (Virginia and the Carolinas, together with Metro New York and their adjacent areas, the “Mid-Atlantic”).

business_model.claim: Almost all revenue comes from selling five product lines: cement, fly ash, aggregates, ready-mix concrete and concrete block.
quotes: Substantially all of the Company’s revenue is derived from sales of cement, fly ash, aggregates, ready-mix concrete and concrete block.

business_model.basis: stated in the P3 revenue-by-product table
business_model.claim: In 2025, consolidated revenue by product was: ready-mix concrete 745,896, cement $626,394, concrete block 147,655, aggregates 115,328 and fly ash 28,607, for a total of $1,664,188 (table in thousands).

business_model.basis: stated in P1 and in the P3 segment revenue table
business_model.claim: The company reports two segments, Florida and Mid-Atlantic. In 2025, segment external revenue was $1,024,415 for Florida and 639,773 for Mid-Atlantic (table in thousands).
quotes: Due to the regional nature of our business, we report our operating results in two reportable segments: Florida and Mid-Atlantic.

business_model.claim: The asset base includes two cement plants, three marine import terminals, 82 ready-mix locations and 22 distribution hubs.
quotes: We operate and maintain two cement plants, three multi-product marine import terminals, seven active mine locations, 82 ready-mix locations with 96 batch plants, eight concrete block locations with 13 production lines, seven fly ash plants and 22 distribution hubs that can handle various combinations of our products.

business_model.claim: The two cement plants have current capacity of 2.4 million tons at Pennsuco in Florida and 1.5 million tons at Roanoke in Virginia, with expansions planned by 2030.
quotes: Our Pennsuco plant currently has a cement production capacity of 2.4 million tons, which, through ongoing focused and strategic investments, we expect will increase to over 2.9 million tons by 2030.
Our Roanoke Plant’s current cement production capacity is 1.5 million tons, and investment is underway with the goal of increasing production capacity to 1.8 million tons by 2030.

business_model.claim: Imported cement adds to own production. The Port Tampa Bay Terminal has averaged over 750,000 tons of imported cement a year.
quotes: Our Port Tampa Bay Terminal has also averaged over 750,000 tons of imported cement annually over the last three years, with an ability to manage approximately 2.5 million tons of cement annually.

business_model.claim: Vertical integration means internally produced cement and aggregates supply the company's own ready-mix and block operations. In 2025, Florida eliminated (230,637) of internal trading (table in thousands).
quotes: Our ready-mix business is fully back-integrated, with access to a strategically-located and reliable supply of primary raw materials, mainly cement and aggregate needed for concrete production.

business_model.claim: Customers are mainly in construction: residential, public infrastructure and large-scale projects. Concrete block is also sold through retail home improvement stores and masonry contractors.
quotes: Our business is largely dependent on demand for residential construction, public spending levels for infrastructure and large-scale projects.
The 13 flexible production units are strategically located throughout our markets to support over 200 retail home improvement stores and key masonry contractors.

business_model.claim: Sales run on customer Orders that set pre-determined prices for a period. Customers can generally cancel these Orders at any time.
quotes: Orders specify products, contractual terms and conditions, estimated quantities, and pre-determined prices over established time periods.
The contracts can generally be cancelled with or without cause at any time, with each party having responsibility for any rights and obligations accrued up to the time of termination.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by construction activity, infrastructure development and urbanization. Pricing depends on the balance of supply and demand and on service.
quotes: Revenue is primarily driven by factors such as construction activity levels, infrastructure development and urbanization trends, which influence the demand for our products.
Product pricing is influenced by supply/demand balances, product performance, reliability and service offerings.

business_model.claim: Competition is largely on price, and products are fairly commoditized. This limits pricing power.
quotes: Competition in these segments is based largely on price and on the quality of the material, service provided, logistics and innovative solutions offered.

business_model.claim: In 2025, revenue rose $29.8 million, or 2%. Higher prices for aggregates and ready-mix concrete and higher aggregates volumes were partly offset by lower cement and concrete block volumes.
quotes: Revenue increased $29.8 million, or 2%, for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, primarily as a result of increases in product pricing for aggregates and ready-mix concrete and increase in aggregates sales volumes partially offset by decreases in sales volumes for cement and concrete block.

business_model.claim: In 2025, external volumes rose 37% in aggregates and 24% in fly ash, and fell 2% in both concrete block and cement.
quotes: External sales volumes increased by 37% in aggregate, 24% in fly ash, remained flat in ready-mix concrete and declined by 2% in concrete block, and 2% in cement for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Sales are seasonal and depend on weather. Mid-Atlantic sales are typically lower in the first and fourth quarters.
quotes: Accordingly, we typically experience a decrease in sales in our Mid-Atlantic reportable segment during the first and fourth quarters reflecting the effect of the winter season in North America and an increase in sales in the second and third quarters reflecting the effect of the summer season in North American markets.

business_model.claim: Operations are geographically concentrated, with about 60% in Florida.
quotes: Currently, approximately 60% of our operations are concentrated in Florida.

business_model.basis: stated in the P3 results table and narrative
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold is the largest cost: (1,229,202) against revenue of $1,664,188 in 2025 (table in thousands). It moves with raw material, labor and energy prices.
quotes: Our cost of goods sold is directly affected by fluctuations in raw materials costs, labor costs and energy prices.

business_model.claim: Cement making is energy intensive, and the company does not use long-term hedges against energy price swings.
quotes: Cement production consumes a large quantity of energy, especially for the kilning and grinding processes.
Risks related to fluctuations in energy and fuel costs are increased due to the fact we do not use any long-term hedging instruments to mitigate the effects of such fluctuations.

business_model.claim: The products are heavy and expensive to move, so freight is a major cost and markets are local around production sites.
quotes: Due to their size and weight, our products are costly and difficult to transport efficiently.
Because of the nature of the products, the freight costs can quickly surpass production costs.

business_model.claim: The key raw material, limestone, comes mainly from owned reserves next to the cement plants.
quotes: While the primary source of the key raw material of limestone is from owned reserves adjacent to our cement plants, there can be no assurance that we will be able to maintain or renew these land and mining rights or that we will have similar cost containment for other inputs used in the production process.

business_model.claim: The business is capital intensive. Net capital expenditures were $163.3 million in 2025, and depreciation, depletion and amortization was 108,716 (table in thousands).
quotes: In the fiscal years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, our net capital expenditures were $118.6 million, $137.3 million and $163.3 million, respectively.

business_model.claim: The company sells trade receivables to a special purpose entity at a discount, which recurs as a cost: (4,012) in 2025 (table in thousands).
quotes: The Company recognizes a fair value loss when it sells its trade accounts receivable to a Special Purpose Entity (“SPE”) at a discount.

business_model.claim: Below operating income, Euro-denominated borrowings create foreign exchange swings that derivatives offset. In 2025 there was an FX loss of (45,101) and a derivative gain of 41,841 (table in thousands).
quotes: The derivatives are used to fix the U.S. dollar cash flows associated with Euro denominated borrowings and to mitigate the impact of U.S. dollar/Euro exchange rate variations on other short-term obligations.

business_model.claim: The company is a controlled subsidiary of Titan SA, which owns about 87% of its shares. It depends on Titan SA's SAP system.
quotes: As of the date of this Annual Report, Titan SA beneficially owns approximately 87% of our common shares.

We are dependent on the SAP license and system of Titan SA and we lack complete control over system updates, maintenance schedules and overall system management, which could lead to delays or disruptions that impact our operations.

business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, Mid-Atlantic revenue rose 22.5%, mainly because of about $30 million of revenue from the acquired Keystone assets.
quotes: The 22.5% year-over-year increase in revenue was primarily due to approximately $30 million of revenue from the acquired Keystone assets, higher pricing and volume in ready-mix concrete partially offset by lower volumes in the segment’s legacy cement operations.

business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, a soft residential market, record rainfall and job site labor shortages hurt Florida, and segment revenue fell to $249,016 from $263,325 (table in thousands).
quotes: While infrastructure demand remained resilient across Titan America’s markets, deteriorating conditions in an already soft residential sector weighed heavily on performance, particularly in Florida.

business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, higher energy costs and an unplanned outage at Roanoke raised costs. Cost of goods sold was (358,139) against (309,209) a year earlier, and gross profit fell to 103,503 from 127,640 (table in thousands).
quotes: A combination of heightened market headwinds, increased energy costs, and unfavorable weather conditions pressured margins during the third quarter.

In addition, the Mid-Atlantic business segment was impacted by an unplanned maintenance outage at the Roanoke Cement plant during the quarter, which reduced cement volumes and increased operating costs.

business_model.claim: Management is running a cost program, Project Cornerstone, which it says saved about $20 million year-to-date in 2026.
quotes: Project Cornerstone has already generated approximately $20 million in cost savings year-to-date in 2026 and it is expected to deliver at a run-rate exceeding $50 million by year-end 2029.

growth_thesis.claim: Funding capacity improved after the 2025 IPO. Net Debt fell to 250,663 from 448,059 (table in thousands), and the Ratio of Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell to 0.6x from 1.2x.
Funding growth internally depends on cash generation, which weakened in 2026. Nine-month 2026 free cash flow was $67,374 against $94,395 (table in thousands of US$), a change of (28.6)%.

Underlying demand depends on residential construction and on public infrastructure spending. Infrastructure demand was resilient in Q3 2026, but the residential sector deteriorated, especially in Florida.
quotes: Our business is largely dependent on demand for residential construction, public spending levels for infrastructure and large-scale projects.
While infrastructure demand remained resilient across Titan America’s markets, deteriorating conditions in an already soft residential sector weighed heavily on performance, particularly in Florida.

growth_thesis.claim: Florida is the condition that matters most. About 60% of operations are there, and Q3 2026 Florida revenue fell to $249.0 million from $263.3 million.
quotes: Currently, approximately 60% of our operations are concentrated in Florida.

The Florida segment generated revenue of $249.0 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $263.3 million in the prior year quarter with lower ready-mix concrete and cement sales volumes and lower cement and concrete block pricing not being fully offset by favorable ready-mix concrete sales pricing, and aggregates sales volumes.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P8 and P5 as management outlook
growth_thesis.claim: Management cut its 2026 growth outlook. It moved from high single digit revenue growth in July 2026 to mid-single-digit growth in November 2026, with Adjusted EBITDA Margin expected to decline by approximately 250 to 300 basis points.
quotes: We now expect high single digit revenue growth versus 2025, including the contribution from Keystone.
Including the contribution from Keystone, we now expect mid-single-digit revenue growth compared to 2025.
We also anticipate Adjusted EBITDA Margin will decline by approximately 250 to 300 basis points year over year.

growth_thesis.claim: For revenue growth to turn into earnings growth, energy and input costs must stay manageable or be passed on to customers. Higher energy and materials costs lowered Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, and Net Income fell to $39.8 million from $57.4 million.
quotes: Increases or significant fluctuations in energy and fuel costs, freight rates or other transportation costs could adversely affect our results of operations, business and financial condition, especially if we are unable to pass along higher input costs to our customers.
A combination of increasing market headwinds, and higher materials and energy costs negatively impacted Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter compared to the same period of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P5 as a management expectation
growth_thesis.claim: Cost savings are a supporting earnings lever. Project Cornerstone generated approximately $20 million of savings year-to-date in 2026 and is expected to reach a run-rate exceeding $50 million by year-end 2029.
quotes: Project Cornerstone has already generated approximately $20 million in cost savings year-to-date in 2026 and it is expected to deliver at a run-rate exceeding $50 million by year-end 2029.

material_events.claim: Titan America completed its IPO of 24,000,000 common shares at $16.00 per share, generating proceeds of approximately $136.8 million after underwriting discounts and commissions.
quotes: On February 10, 2025, we completed our initial public offering of 24,000,000 common shares (the “IPO”).
The common shares were sold at an offering price of $16.00 per share, generating proceeds of approximately $136.8 million, after deducting underwriting discounts and other commissions.

material_events.claim: The STET segment was divested to Titan Cement Netherlands B.V., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the parent Titan SA.
quotes: The STET segment was divested on January 1, 2025 to Titan Cement Netherlands B.V., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Titan SA.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited items; the closing date and price are not given
material_events.claim: The company completed its acquisition of Keystone Cement. The acquired assets contributed revenue to the Mid-Atlantic segment in Q3 2026.
quotes: Following our recently completed acquisition of Keystone Cement, we have updated our full year 2026 outlook for the Company.

The 22.5% year-over-year increase in revenue was primarily due to approximately $30 million of revenue from the acquired Keystone assets, higher pricing and volume in ready-mix concrete partially offset by lower volumes in the segment’s legacy cement operations.

material_events.claim: The company lowered its full-year 2026 outlook. It now expects mid-single-digit revenue growth, down from high single digit growth in July. It expects Adjusted EBITDA margin to decline by approximately 250 to 300 basis points.
quotes: Including the contribution from Keystone, we now expect mid-single-digit revenue growth compared to 2025.
We also anticipate Adjusted EBITDA Margin will decline by approximately 250 to 300 basis points year over year.
We now expect high single digit revenue growth versus 2025, including the contribution from Keystone.

material_events.claim: An unplanned maintenance outage at the Roanoke Cement plant during Q3 2026 reduced cement volumes and increased operating costs.
quotes: In addition, the Mid-Atlantic business segment was impacted by an unplanned maintenance outage at the Roanoke Cement plant during the quarter, which reduced cement volumes and increased operating costs.

material_events.claim: Q3 2026 net income fell to $39.8 million from $57.4 million in Q3 2025. Management cites margin pressure, especially in Florida.
quotes: Net Income of $39.8 million, compared to $57.4 million in Q3 2025
